correctness.rationale: For n≥3 the two tagged-pair disagreement probabilities obey the displayed 2×2 ODE with initial values (1,0); integrating yields exact E N_n=2(n−1)/(n+2). The terminal opinion martingale gives E U_n=(n−1)(n−2)/(2n(n+2)). The total mutant-count process has equal birth/death rates and the quadratic stopped potential satisfies Lg≤−i, proving the all-future rare-return upper bound. The n=2 case is checked directly, and k=⌊√n⌋ gives convergence in probability and a positive extra expectation; every logical step is finite-state and exact. Independent labelled-state generator checks n=2..9 and separate event aggregation checks n=3..17; finite tests are not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: For a natural and canonical absorbing stochastic dynamical system, the theorem sharply separates typical founder paths from expectation: N_n converges in probability to one although the mean converges to two. A separately proved all-future rare-event bound implies conditional upward-reversal counts have mean at least of square-root order, resolving where the excess expectation hides. The exact finite-size formulas and quantitative mechanism are substantial, not arbitrary small numerical slices; the statement neither relies on unknown novelty of the zero-flip probability nor asserts an unproved sharp tail.
